chunks: Safwan narrated from Yahya al-Azraq, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: A man performed the sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa, completing three or four circuits, then urinated, then completed his sa‘i without wudu (ablution).
So he عليه السلام said: 'There is no harm, though if he had completed his rites with wudu (ablution), that would have been more preferable to me.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two points between which sa‘i is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwa, the other point of the sa‘i rite
key_terms.سَعَى: performed the sa‘i rite between al-Safa and al-Marwa
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is not objectionable or invalid
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), ritual washing before acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Is wudu required to complete sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa in hajj or 'umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that completing the sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwa without wudu (ablution), after having broken it by urination, does not invalidate the rite. At the same time, the Imam عليه السلام indicates that performing one's manasik in a state of wudu is preferable and more beloved.
